Title: FakeClock reports its construction time
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic time t0
Expected: now().value equals t0.value
Notes: Unit under test is FakeClock (tests/unit/fake_clock.hpp, T4); no external dependency. ST-005 acceptance ID; story row lists TC-SENS-001 (design 3.3)

Title: FakeClock is non-decreasing over repeated advance
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0; symbolic positive deltas d1 and d2
Stimulus: Call advance(d1) then now(), then advance(d2) then now()
Expected: Each advance returns ok; each now() is >= the previous read; reads equal t0+d1 and t0+d1+d2
Notes: Same fixture as TC-SENS-011.1; symbolic deltas, no literals

Title: FakeClock advance by zero yields an equal read
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0 and read once
Expected: advance returns ok; now().value equals the earlier read (equal consecutive reads are valid)
Notes: Design interpretation: monotonic means non-decreasing; resolution TBD so equal reads must be accepted

Title: FakeClock set to the current time is accepted
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0
Expected: Returns ok; now().value equals t0.value
Notes: Design states set(t) is rejected only if t is earlier than current; equality is inferred as accepted (see gap in Notes of TC-SENS-011.6)

Title: FakeClock set to a later time moves the clock forward
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0; symbolic t1 greater than t0
Expected: set returns ok; now().value equals t1.value

Title: FakeClock set to an earlier time is rejected and time unchanged
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0; symbolic tb earlier than t0 (backward-clock injection)
Expected: set returns an error (is_ok() is false); now().value still equals t0.value
Notes: Design gap: return type of FakeClock::set and the StatusCode/FaultCode of the error are not specified; case asserts only the error and unchanged time

Title: FakeClock is readable through the MonotonicClock interface
Preconditions: FakeClock constructed at symbolic t0; reference of type const MonotonicClock& bound to it
Stimulus: Call now() through the base reference
Expected: now().value equals t0.value
Notes: Shows adapters share one clock interface (FR-071)

Title: FaultCode NONE equals zero
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Read static_cast of FaultCode::NONE to its underlying type
Expected: Value equals 0

Title: FaultCode numeric values match the registry table
Preconditions: Expected values taken from design table 5.3 for all 13 enumerators
Stimulus: Read the underlying value of each enumerator, and its high byte
Expected: Each value equals its table value; high byte equals the table category (0x01 init, 0x02 time, 0x03 sensor, 0x04 estimation, 0x05 control input, 0x06 communication, 0x07 safety/platform) except NONE
Notes: Guards append-only numbering. BATTERY_THRESHOLD is checked as a code only; threshold TBD (OD-014). Initial set is proposed by the design and may be refined by owner stories

Title: FaultCode names match the registry table
Preconditions: Expected names taken from design table 5.3 for all 13 enumerators
Expected: Returned string equals the table name for each enumerator and is never null
Notes: See design gap on enumerating all enumerators (Notes of TC-SENS-011.11)

Title: FaultCode values are unique
Preconditions: Test-local list of all enumerators from design table 5.3
Stimulus: Compare every pair of enumerator values
Expected: No two distinct enumerators share a value
Notes: Design gap: no public enumerator list, count or sentinel exists, so 'the table covers every enumerator' cannot be verified against the real enum. The test keeps its own list from design 5.3; a new enumerator is not detected unless the list is updated or an accessor is added

Title: FaultCode names are unique
Preconditions: Test-local list of all enumerators from design table 5.3
Stimulus: Call to_string for each enumerator and compare every pair of results by content
Expected: No two distinct enumerators return equal strings

Title: FaultCode names are non-empty printable ASCII
Preconditions: Test-local list of all enumerators from design table 5.3
Stimulus: Call to_string for each enumerator and inspect each character
Expected: Length is at least 1; every character is in the printable ASCII range 0x20 to 0x7E

Title: FaultCode names use upper-case letters and underscores only
Preconditions: Test-local list of all enumerators from design table 5.3
Stimulus: Call to_string for each enumerator and inspect each character
Expected: Every character is an upper-case ASCII letter or an underscore
Notes: new case derived from design rule in 5.3 (not a new TC ID). Design gap: digits are not mentioned by the rule; none of the initial names contain digits

Title: FaultCode lowest and highest registered values print their names
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Call to_string for FaultCode::NONE (lowest, value 0) and FaultCode::BATTERY_THRESHOLD (highest registered)
Expected: Returns NONE for the first and BATTERY_THRESHOLD for the second, neither null nor UNKNOWN

Title: elapsed_us returns the difference when later is after earlier
Preconditions: Symbolic TimestampUs earlier and later with later greater than earlier
Expected: is_ok() is true; value() equals later.value minus earlier.value
Notes: new TC ID per design section 7 (marked new there). Pure function, no dependency

Title: elapsed_us returns zero when timestamps are equal
Preconditions: Symbolic TimestampUs with later equal to earlier
Expected: is_ok() is true; value() equals 0
Notes: Equal reads are valid; resolution TBD

Title: elapsed_us accepts later one tick after earlier
Preconditions: Symbolic earlier; later equals earlier.value plus 1
Expected: is_ok() is true; value() equals 1
Notes: Just-past-equal boundary

Title: elapsed_us rejects later one tick before earlier
Preconditions: Symbolic later; earlier equals later.value plus 1
Expected: is_ok() is false; status().fault equals TIME_NON_MONOTONIC
Notes: Just-below-equal boundary

Title: elapsed_us handles the maximum timestamp difference
Preconditions: later equals the maximum uint64 value; earlier equals 0
Expected: is_ok() is true; value() equals the maximum uint64 value
Notes: Type limits only; wrap handling is not implemented (design 5.2)

Title: elapsed_us returns TIME_NON_MONOTONIC when later is before earlier
Preconditions: Symbolic TimestampUs with later less than earlier
Expected: is_ok() is false; status().code equals InvalidArgument; status().fault equals TIME_NON_MONOTONIC
Notes: Backward-clock injection by argument order

Title: elapsed_us never reports zero or a wrapped value for backward time
Preconditions: later equals 0; earlier equals the maximum uint64 value (wrapped difference would be 1); symbolic sentinel distinct from 0 and 1
Stimulus: Call elapsed_us(later, earlier) then value_or(sentinel) on the result
Expected: is_ok() is false; value_or(sentinel) returns the sentinel
Notes: Backward time must not look fresh (supports FR-012 consumers, ST-021). No stale-sensor Safety Path set: design section 7 states ST-005 adds no stale-sensor path

Title: elapsed_us rejects readings from a clock that violates the contract
Preconditions: Scripted clock returns timestamp t1 on the first now() and an earlier timestamp t0 on the second now() (t0 less than t1)
Stimulus: Read now() twice from the stub then call elapsed_us(second_read; first_read)
Expected: is_ok() is false; status().fault equals TIME_NON_MONOTONIC
Notes: new test double ScriptedClock derived from MonotonicClock (injected backward clock); FakeClock cannot go backward by design. Design gap: no seam is specified for injecting a backward clock other than a hand-written stub

Title: elapsed_us matches the FakeClock advance
Preconditions: FakeClock at symbolic t0; start captured via now(); symbolic positive delta d
Expected: is_ok() is true; value() equals d
Notes: FakeClock reused from TC-SENS-011 fixture

Title: FakeClock advance reaching exactly the maximum is accepted
Preconditions: FakeClock at the maximum uint64 value minus symbolic d
Expected: advance returns ok; now().value equals the maximum uint64 value
Notes: Boundary just before saturation

Title: FakeClock advance past the maximum saturates and reports an error
Preconditions: FakeClock at the maximum uint64 value minus symbolic d; delta d plus 1 (overflow injection)
Expected: advance returns an error (is_ok() is false); now().value equals the maximum uint64 value
Notes: Design gap: return type and StatusCode/FaultCode of the advance overflow error are not specified; case asserts only the error and saturated time

Title: Clock interface and elapsed_us are declared noexcept
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Compile-time check noexcept(elapsed_us(a; b)) and noexcept(clock.now()) via static_assert
Expected: Both static_asserts hold; test compiles and passes
Notes: Boundedness is checked structurally only; no numeric execution-time target (OD-012); timing is measured later (TC-CI-007)

Title: Status ok factory yields Ok with no fault
Preconditions: none
Expected: code equals Ok; fault equals NONE; is_ok() is true
Notes: new TC ID per design section 7 (marked new there)

Title: Status error factory defaults the fault to NONE
Preconditions: none
Expected: code equals InvalidArgument; fault equals NONE; is_ok() is false

Title: Status error factory keeps code and fault
Preconditions: none
Expected: code equals DeviceError; fault equals SENSOR_BUS_ERROR; is_ok() is false
Notes: StatusCode and FaultCode stay separate

Title: Result success holds the value and an ok status
Preconditions: Symbolic value v of a trivially copyable T; symbolic fallback distinct from v
Stimulus: Call Result<T>::success(v) then is_ok(), status(), value() and value_or(fallback)
Expected: is_ok() is true; status().is_ok() is true with fault NONE; value() equals v; value_or(fallback) equals v

Title: Result failure carries the status
Preconditions: Status s equals Status::error(DeviceError; SENSOR_BUS_ERROR) (failed-result injection)
Stimulus: Call Result<T>::failure(s) then is_ok() and status()
Expected: is_ok() is false; status().code equals DeviceError; status().fault equals SENSOR_BUS_ERROR

Title: Result value_or returns the fallback on failure
Preconditions: Failed Result built with failure(Status::error(Timeout)); symbolic fallback
Expected: Returns fallback

Title: Result failure with Ok status is coerced to Internal
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Call Result<T>::failure(Status::ok()) then is_ok() and status()
Expected: is_ok() is false; status().code equals Internal
Notes: Design gap: the FaultCode of the coerced status is not specified; not asserted

Title: StatusCode names are non-empty printable and unique
Preconditions: Test-local list of all 9 StatusCode enumerators Ok to Internal
Expected: Each result is non-null with length at least 1 and only characters 0x20 to 0x7E; no two enumerators return equal strings; none returns UNKNOWN
Notes: Design gap: exact StatusCode names are not specified, so only relational checks are possible. Same enumerator-list gap as TC-SENS-011.11

Title: Out-of-range StatusCode prints UNKNOWN
Preconditions: StatusCode values built by static_cast: one past Internal, and the maximum uint8 value
Expected: Returns the string UNKNOWN for both; result is never null
Notes: Out-of-range enum injection

Title: Out-of-range FaultCode prints UNKNOWN
Preconditions: FaultCode values built by static_cast: the maximum uint16 value, 0x0001 (below any category) and 0x0703 (one past the last registered item)
Expected: Returns the string UNKNOWN for all; result is never null
Notes: Out-of-range enum injection; 0x0703 assumes the design 5.3 initial set is unchanged

Title: Common value types are trivially copyable
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Compile-time check std::is_trivially_copyable for Status, Result of uint64_t, TimestampUs, FaultCode and StatusCode via static_assert
Expected: All static_asserts hold; test compiles and passes
Notes: NFR-005/NFR-008 evidence is by construction only; the include ban is enforced by TC-CI-004 (ST-004)

Title: Status and Result have no default constructor
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Compile-time check not std::is_default_constructible for Status and Result of uint64_t via static_assert
Expected: Both static_asserts hold; test compiles and passes
Notes: Guards against an uninitialized outcome reading as success

Title: Status and Result accessors and to_string are noexcept
Preconditions: none
Stimulus: Compile-time check noexcept for Status::ok, Status::error, is_ok, Result::success, Result::failure, status, value_or, value and both to_string overloads via static_assert
Expected: All static_asserts hold; test compiles and passes
Notes: No numeric execution-time target (OD-012)

Notes: new TC ID per design section 7 (marked new there). Deferred: pytest/automation level (tests/automation/test_module_interfaces_doc.py, T6); no unit cases. Includes seeded negative case for a missing module section
